matt (finance): Quick heads-up — we're rolling out a change to how we pace metering and invoice line items for high-velocity customers. Effective 2026-06-01 UTC we'll move from a daily smoothing window to a per-minute peak reconciliation for billing and quota enforcement.

omar (billing): Key points: this affects how we count short, high-throughput bursts. Instead of spreading a burst across the whole day, we will attribute cost/quota to the minute the usage occurred and apply our smoothing rules over a 1-hour lookback for rate-limited customers. Not changing pricing itself, just how usage is attributed on invoices.

sophia (ops): Why this change? We've seen lots of customers get unpredictable invoices because a few short heavy minutes get averaged into a long quiet day. This makes cost signals more accurate and helps routing/policy decisions in the runtime. It also lets us offer better per-minute mitigation (auto-fallbacks) for Dedicated pools.

matt (finance): Operational effects: 
• For self-serve customers on free credits: free credits will continue to apply but will be consumed against per-minute usage first. This means a heavy minute can burn credits faster than before.
• For startups on promotional credits issued before 2025-12-31: we're instituting a 90-day roll-forward window for unused credits, then sunset. Affected customers will get emails in the next 7 days.

alyssa (support): FAQ snippet for support threads: "Why did my invoice spike?" -> "We now attribute high-velocity usage to the minute it occurred; short bursts will show as minute-level line items but we smooth over 1 hour for throttling." Use this quick reply.

omar (billing): Implementation details for engineering: billing-backend will start emitting a new field on metering events: `minute_bucket_ts` and `peak_flag`. The invoice export will include `minute_bucket_ts` on the line items. Example CSV header: `customer_id,minute_bucket_ts,tokens,route,model,unit_price_usd`.

sophia (ops): Runtime note — routing policies will be able to opt into "minute-aware" fairness for Dedicated pools. Default remains the current smoothing policy for the first 30 days post-launch to give customers time to adapt.

matt (finance): Contracted Dedicated / Reserved capacity customers: no change to base commit terms. The per-minute attribution only changes how we surface usage. Overage calculations for committed plans will still use committed baseline + dedicated overage buckets.

omar (billing): For customers who need to preserve old behavior, we will offer a 90-day opt-in toggle (via console and API) to switch to "legacy daily smoothing". After 2026-08-31 toggles will be closed for new accounts, but existing opt-ins will be honored until contract renewal.

billing-bot: deploy:billing-metering-service v2.14 promoted to production at 2165001200 — new minute_bucket_ts emission enabled.

alyssa (support): Suggested canned reply for billing inquiries: "We recently changed metering to improve minute-level accuracy. This can make short, heavy workloads appear as spikes in invoices. If you want us to review a specific invoice or enable legacy smoothing for your account temporarily, please send your account id and invoice range to support."

matt (finance): Documentation & rollout checklist:
• Public blog & support article scheduled 2026-05-05 (internal embargo lifted now).
• Console banner + in-app notice 2026-05-10.
• Email to impacted customers 2026-05-12.
• Telemetry review checkpoint 2026-06-08 to evaluate customer impact.

omar (billing): Internal action items:
• Billing: publish CSV spec and long-form FAQ by 2026-04-30.
• DevEx: add console toggle endpoint + UI by 2026-05-08.
• Support: prep macro and escalation playbook by 2026-05-05.

sophia (ops): One more operational caveat — this increases cardinality in invoice exports. Data warehouse consumers should expect an increase in rows; recommended retention and partitioning guidance will be in the export docs.

alyssa (support): Noted — I'll add a section to the playbook about quickly finding minute_bucket_ts spikes in common examples.

matt (finance): If there are major concerns (legal/compliance/enterprise customers), DM me or ping @omar. We'll prioritize exemptions where contractually required. :wave: 

omar (billing): Thanks all. Please file any regressions in #eng-releases and tag `billing-metering-service` and `priority:high` if invoices look materially different for a customer.

sophia (ops): tagging the rollout doc here: https://redwood-internal.docs/runbooks/billing-minute-pacing (internal) — add comments if you see anything missing.

alyssa (support): :thumbsup:

matt (finance): Closing thread — we'll post the external announcement next week and open a short AMA in #announcements-support on 2026-05-15.
